SongComments.SongComment: This short tutorial song demonstrates the possibilities of cross-track routing for injecting life into otherwise plain sounds.
The first pattern plays the drumloop and bass sounds in their standard, unaltered forms.

In the second pattern you can hear how the bassline is modulated by the drumloop's amplitude. This is done by linking the first track's Signal Follower to the second track's Hydra Device (which in turn is also linked to several other parameters). Notice that the Gainer appears after the Signal Follower, so that the drumloop is still used for modulation even though it falls silent afterwards.

A similiar effect could have been achieved by linking the Signal Follower to a single Filter. But what this tutorial shows is that it is possible to modulate numerous parameters using a single source, without the need to create multiple automations.
The third pattern un-mutes the drumloop, allowing you to hear exactly how its rhythm is affecting the bassline as they play side by side.

Note: The Signal Follower cannot affect devices that appear on tracks to the left of its own host track. It is also unable to control effects on the same track as itself, if that device appears before it in the DSP chain. Such tracks and effects will show in the "Dest." box with the suffix: "(N/A)" (i.e. Not Available). If you want to affect a track or device that currently shows as "(N/A)", then simply reorder the tracks or effects so that the Signal Follower appears before (to the left of) the desired parameter.
